result.evidence: The dependency facts hold: ht-qhz.3 and ht-qhz.2.1 each depend on ht-qhz.1, which names the peer actor-route/classify_original_actor seam and requires classification before new journal retry (artifact.md:1048,779,1119). The load-bearing premise that completing ht-qhz.1 necessarily requires landed peer actor execution does not hold against the combined contract. The root assigns this leaf topology types and inert dispatch/signatures (line 57); the task explicitly says "Land only compilable additive BootstrapPlan/DeliveryPlan, state/result types and inert protocol/CLI/journal dispatch wiring" and "inert-by-default" (line 1119). This permits the shared neutral contract to land with execution refused until canonical guards and original-actor integration exist; classification-before-retry is an execution ordering invariant, not permission to run an unclassified retry. Root line 101 explicitly limits unavailable shared boundaries to their integration leaf, and ht-qhz.6 expressly gates exact human integration on named peer source availability (line 935). The assertion that no independently completable contract prerequisite/equivalent mechanism exists overlooks the designated inert contract itself. Final authority integration (ht-qhz.19, line 378) and integration sweep (ht-qhz.20, line 229) enforce origin classification before completed cleanup and consume the executing leaves. Separately, ht-qhz.2.1 alone expressly waits for actual migration0026/0027 before editing0028 and states that independent ready work proceeds (line 779). No external library/API premise is needed for this structural verdict.
